note: THE-347 fixes a React error #31 that took /admin/blog down entirely: a Firestore Timestamp reached JSX and the error boundary took the screen. THE DEFECT WAS THE CATCH, NOT THE PARSE. AdminBlog's own formatDate did new Date(value) - an Invalid Date for an object - and Intl.DateTimeFormat.format(InvalidDate) THROWS RangeError rather than returning a string, so the catch fired and returned dateString: THE INPUT, which was never a string. That is the Silent-Failure Rule in its most literal form, except the quiet lie was loud enough to take the whole screen. THE CAUSE IS ONE DAY OLD AND IT IS #490's: blog_posts has three writers, and AdminBlogPostEditor and /api/blog/generate both write new Date().toISOString() while handleShareToBlogDraft - added by THE-346 in #490, blamed to that commit - wrote serverTimestamp(). The interface declared createdAt: string and doc.data() was cast straight to it, so TypeScript asserted a claim the data does not support and every consumer downstream was wrong with no compiler error. REPRODUCED BEFORE ANYTHING WAS CHANGED: mounting the real AdminBlog with a {seconds, nanoseconds} createdAt throws 'Objects are not valid as a React child (found: object with keys {seconds, nanoseconds})' - verbatim the founder's screenshot - and restoring the old formatter turns 12 of this ticket's tests red. THE ANSWER TO AN UNPARSEABLE DATE IS A VISIBLE PLACEHOLDER, an em-dash, and the other three were considered and rejected on the record: returning the input is this bug; throwing takes a screen down over one bad row; an empty string hides the failure from the reader, which is the same quiet lie one layer along. NewsletterCampaigns already answers an unparseable date with that exact character, so it is the repo's convention rather than a new invention. The formatter is built on tsMillis so the label and the sort can never disagree about what a value MEANS, and it is total by construction - every path returns a string, and the resolve is INSIDE the guard because tsMillis calls toMillis() and that call can itself throw. ONE REPRESENTATION, AND IT IS THE ISO STRING: the other two writers, the interface, and the public /blog/[id] <time dateTime> attribute and schema.org JSON-LD all require ISO 8601, where a Timestamp serialises as [object Object]. Firestore also orders across types by TYPE first, so a mixed field sorts wrong before it renders wrong. WHAT IS REPORTED AND NOT FIXED: documents already written by #490's path still hold Timestamps, and whether to migrate them is the founder's call - the read path now renders both correctly, so no migration is needed to bring the screen back. Also reported, not fixed: the U+26A1 in Generate Now's label, the GOLD inline style, AdminBlog's two hand-written empty states, and four uncaught Intl helpers elsewhere that would throw RangeError on the same data. NO firestore.rules CHANGE IS NEEDED AND NONE IS MADE, and this record carries NO rules digest - THE-333 and THE-341 each spelling one is what turned THE-325 red, twice. No new token, component or dependency; the lockfile THE-274 pins is untouched.

entries.why: THE-347 ADDS this file and it is the whole fix at the render boundary: formatFirestoreDate, which is TOTAL - every path returns a string and no path can return the value it was given. That property is the ticket: a formatter declared to return a string that hands back its input on failure is what put a Timestamp object into JSX. It is built on tsMillis rather than on a second parser so the formatter and sortByTime can never disagree about what a value means, and the tsMillis call sits INSIDE the try because tsMillis invokes toMillis() and a Timestamp-shaped object can throw from it - a formatter that throws while trying to be safe is the same outage by another route, and this ticket's own guard caught that before merge. The final typeof check is what keeps the signature true against a future edit. UNPARSEABLE_DATE is an em-dash and the reasoning for choosing it over an empty string or a throw is written out in the file, with FirestoreDate exported so a screen has an honest type to declare a date field with.

THE-347 changes ONE thing here and it is a keyword: TimestampLike is EXPORTED. Nothing about the type moved, no function body changed, and tsMillis and sortByTime are byte-identical in behaviour. It was file-private, so firestore-date.ts could not name the very shape it exists to render and a screen wanting to be honest about its data had no type to be honest with - which is how blog_posts.createdAt came to be declared string while one of its three writers wrote a Timestamp. The doc comment records that, so the export reads as load-bearing rather than incidental.

THE-347 owns this change and it is the CRASH ITSELF. formatDate no longer carries its own try/catch returning dateString; it delegates to the shared total formatter, and createdAt/updatedAt/publishedAt are declared FirestoreDate instead of string because that declaration was a lie the compiler agreed with. Both render sites - the phone card list and the desktop table - were affected and both are fixed by the one change, because they call the same helper. NOTHING ELSE MOVED: the onSnapshot read, sortByTime(fetchedPosts, 'createdAt', 'desc'), the delete flow, the search and category filters, and the whole automation panel are untouched, and the panel's hour select, timezone, topic hint, stats row and both buttons are asserted still present. nextScheduledAt's isNaN guard is untouched and still renders through toLocaleDateString, and it is pinned as a no-regression including the case where it holds a Timestamp. TWO THINGS ARE REPORTED AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED: the U+26A1 in Generate Now's label - the emoji sweep is per-ticket, no existing guard sweeps this file, so removing it is pre-existing work and its own ticket, and it is RECORDED here so a second emoji fails - and style={{backgroundColor: GOLD}}, an inline style over a hardcoded constant, which #482 made a palette question rather than a render one. The two hand-written 'No posts found' empty states are likewise reported rather than rebuilt on the empty primitive.

THE-347 owns this change and it is the SAME defect on the member-facing blog, found by sweeping rather than by a report. This file reads the same blog_posts collection and carried a byte-for-byte copy of the broken helper - catch (e) { return dateString; } - behind three render sites. It is the shared formatter now, with the same type widening. TWO MORE BUGS SURFACED ONLY BECAUSE THE TYPE STOPPED LYING, and both are fixed here: the scheduled-post filter compared publishedAt <= now LEXICOGRAPHICALLY, which is meaningful only while every document holds an ISO string and against an object compares '[object Object]' so a scheduled post leaks out early; and the sort did new Date(x).getTime(), which is NaN for a Timestamp so every comparison involving one returned NaN and those posts stayed wherever they happened to be. Both go through tsMillis now, which is what sortByTime has been doing correctly all along. No Firestore path, query or handler moved.

THE-347 owns this change and it is a FOURTH crash site, invisible until the interface stopped claiming these fields were strings. scheduledDate initialised with new Date(post.publishedAt).toISOString().slice(0, 16); for a Timestamp that is new Date(object) - an Invalid Date - and toISOString() on one THROWS RangeError, so merely OPENING a post whose publishedAt was a Timestamp took the editor down. It is a small toDatetimeLocal helper now: never throws, never returns anything but a string, and answers '' when there is no usable date, which is the right empty for a datetime-local input rather than the em-dash a rendered label wants. The UTC-vs-local behaviour of the original is preserved deliberately. The three write paths in this file are untouched and still write new Date().toISOString(), which is the representation blog_posts settles on.

THE-347 owns this change and it is ONE expression: handleShareToBlogDraft writes createdAt as new Date().toISOString() rather than serverTimestamp(). This is the writer that CAUSED the crash - git blames the line to 85345bc, THE-346 in #490, merged the same day the founder photographed the error - and it was the only one of blog_posts' three writers storing an object. Changing it stops new mixed documents being created; it does not repair the ones already written, which is reported as the founder's migration call rather than migrated here. The direction was not a coin flip: the other two writers, the BlogPost interface, and the public /blog/[id] <time dateTime> attribute and schema.org JSON-LD all require ISO 8601, and a Timestamp there serialises as [object Object] into SEO metadata. THE CHANGE IS SCOPED TO blog_posts AND THAT IS ASSERTED: the twelve serverTimestamp() writes belonging to the docs collection are untouched, because docs stores Timestamps consistently and rewriting them would be inventing a second migration. THE-346's own test for this row - one blog_posts document, status draft, publishing nothing - still passes unchanged; it never asserted the shape of createdAt. Nothing else in the file moved: no menu row, no toolbar, no share flow, no Firestore path.
